name: Transactions, Concurrency & Consistency
description: Transactions, Concurrency & Consistency standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-DATA-TX applies.

rules.title: Choose transaction boundaries around business invariants
rules.detail: A transaction should include the minimum set of database changes that must succeed or fail together for one business operation.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Choose transaction boundaries around business invariants.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Choose transaction boundaries around business invariants.

rules.title: Do not hold database transactions across slow external calls
rules.detail: Commit or use an outbox/saga pattern rather than keeping locks open while calling remote services unless explicitly justified.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Do not hold database transactions across slow external calls.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Do not hold database transactions across slow external calls.

rules.title: Select isolation and locking based on concurrency risk
rules.detail: Use database defaults deliberately; use optimistic tokens, unique constraints or row locks for known race conditions.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Select isolation and locking based on concurrency risk.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Select isolation and locking based on concurrency risk.

rules.title: Make retried operations safe
rules.detail: Transactions subject to deadlock/serialization retry must be idempotent or protected from duplicate side effects.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Make retried operations safe.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Make retried operations safe.

rules.title: Use outbox/inbox patterns for database plus messaging consistency
rules.detail: When one logical operation updates durable data and publishes/consumes messages, avoid unsafe dual writes.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Use outbox/inbox patterns for database plus messaging consistency.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Use outbox/inbox patterns for database plus messaging consistency.

rules.title: Test concurrent behavior for critical invariants
rules.detail: Automated tests should exercise duplicate, parallel update and retry scenarios where money, inventory, identity or other critical state is affected.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Test concurrent behavior for critical invariants.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Test concurrent behavior for critical invariants.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-DATA-TX applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Transactions, Concurrency & Consistency to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Transactions, Concurrency & Consistency is applied inconsistently across features
common_issues.cause: The project references the standard but does not resolve concrete ownership, thresholds or verification evidence.
common_issues.solution: Resolve dependencies, record project-specific decisions and include applicable rules in implementation/review checks.

common_issues.issue: Implementation satisfies the happy path but misses Transactions, Concurrency & Consistency failure cases
common_issues.cause: Boundary, retry, security or recovery scenarios were not included in acceptance/test planning.
common_issues.solution: Use the standard rules to add explicit failure/recovery scenarios and verify them before release.
